title: Shifted free graded modules sheafify to twists
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. For every integer $d$, the associated sheaf $\widetilde{S(d)}$ of the graded shift $S(d)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] is isomorphic to the twisting module $\mathcal O_P(d)$ defined by the standard affine cover of [def-sc-p1-standard] and [lem-sc-p1-twist-exists]; consequently the associated sheaf of a finite direct sum of shifts is the corresponding finite direct sum of twists.

proof.text: For each standard chart U_i=D_+(x_i), the definition of the associated sheaf gives Gamma(U_i,~S(d))=(S_{x_i})_d. Multiplication by x_i^{-d} identifies this module with k[x_{1-i}/x_i] and sends the distinguished degree-d element x_i^d to 1; equivalently, x_i^d is a free generator of the restriction of ~S(d) on U_i.

source.place: Definition 01MN (1), Lemma 01M7 (2),(3), specialized to S=k[x_0,x_1] and f=x_i

proof.text: On U_{01}, write t=x_1/x_0. Under the chart identifications from the preceding step, the two generators satisfy x_0^d=(x_0/x_1)^d x_1^d=t^{-d}x_1^d. Thus the transition map for ~S(d) is the transition prescribed in the definition of the twisted module O_P(d). By the existence and uniqueness statement for that glued module, these chart identifications glue to an isomorphism ~S(d) ~= O_P(d).

source.place: Definition 01MN (1) and Lemma 01M7 (2),(3), with the transition relation on D_+(x_0) cap D_+(x_1)

proof.text: For a finite direct sum of shifts, localization and taking the degree-d part commute with finite direct sums, so the associated sheaf is the finite direct sum of the associated sheaves of the summands. Applying the isomorphism of the preceding step to each summand gives the corresponding finite direct sum of twists.
